1) Restate the decision: Propose a tenant-scoped Organization Activity Feed architecture (web feed + streaming API) that integrates with existing microservices and the internal message bus while ensuring regional residency and long-term EU retention.  
2) Assumptions and constraints: existing microservices and bus remain in place; some events lack a unified schema; do not rebuild core platform; EU tenants require 7-year retention and EU-only residency with controlled cross-region access for both data and access logs; infra permits managed multi-region stores but prefers avoiding exotic streaming stacks; must support near-real-time SIEM streaming while preserving strong tenant isolation and audited access.  
3) Key options being considered: A) Event Aggregation Service that normalizes events and writes per-tenant, time-partitioned append-only streams into region-resident read stores and cold archives; B) Query-time aggregation from existing audit/doc stores; C) Lightweight forwarder that pushes raw events to customer SIEMs/endpoints.  
4) Trade-offs: A gives low-latency UI, scalable streaming (tenant-scoped topics, SSE/WebSocket/webhooks), clear regional routing/retention and strong access auditing but adds storage/ops and event duplication; B minimizes new infra but risks high query load, poor latency, and complex cross-region/compliance controls; C reduces our UI burden but fragments schema, pushes security/compliance to customers, and breaks unified retention/audit.  
5) Recommendation and justification: Recommend A — build an Event Aggregation Service that consumes bus events, enforces a canonical schema and tenant+region routing, writes append-only per-tenant time-partitioned streams into managed region-resident read stores (fast indexed shards for paginated UI) and region-specific cold object archives for long retention (EU 7 years), expose paginated REST endpoints for the UI and streaming via tenant-scoped pub/sub topics plus SSE/WebSocket/webhook push with rate-limiting, authenticate streams with tenant-bound strong auth (OAuth2 client credentials ± mTLS) and write immutable, region-resident access logs; this meets low-latency, scalability, and strict compliance requirements while staying within existing microservice architecture.  
6) Follow-ups/validations needed before committing: confirm per-tenant and per-region event volumes and peak rates, precise retention and encryption/compliance details for EU tenants, acceptable streaming protocols and SIEM formats, required auth mechanisms and audit log retention/format, budget for storage/egress and managed pub/sub capacity, and which upstream services will own emitting/annotating canonical event fields.

1) Restate the decision: Architect the Event Aggregation Service to produce tenant- and region-scoped Organization Activity Feeds exposed as (a) paginated UI APIs, (b) HTTPS-based streaming (preferred SSE with long-poll fallback), and (c) secure on-demand bulk exports from region-resident storage while enforcing EU 7-year residency and audited access.  
2) Assumptions and constraints: we must not rework core services, will consume events from the internal bus, infra supports managed multi-region storage and HTTP/2/TLS but no customer-facing brokers, EU tenants require 7-year retention in EU data centers with controlled cross-region access of data and access logs, SIEM consumers prefer HTTPS/SSE, and operational simplicity/managed services are prioritized over exotic new stacks.  
3) Key options being considered: (A) SSE-first Event Aggregation Service that normalizes events, writes append-only per-tenant+region time-partitioned streams to a fast read store and cold archive, and directly serves SSE/WebSocket/SSE-client connections; (B) Webhook/push-only model where service pushes to customer endpoints; (C) Query-time UI over audit/doc stores with export-from-object-store for bulk.

5) Recommendation and justification: Implement A — Event Aggregation Service normalizes events into a canonical schema, routes and writes them into managed region-resident fast read shards (indexed by tenant + time) for paginated UI and into region-specific cold archives (managed object store) for long retention, expose streaming over SSE on HTTPS (HTTP/2) with long-poll fallback and server-side per-tenant backpressure/rate-limiting, authenticate streams and export requests with tenant-scoped OAuth2 client credentials plus optional mTLS and short-lived signed JWTs; generate bulk export manifests and time-limited signed URLs for region-resident object store objects (per-tenant, per-window) and record every access in immutable region-resident access logs replicated to the appropriate compliance store.  
6) Follow-ups/validations needed: confirm peak and sustained per-tenant/event volumes and export sizes, exact EU encryption/sovereignty/encryption key management and audit-log retention requirements, acceptable streaming formats/payload schema for SIEM, precise auth requirements (OAuth scopes, mTLS), retention/archival lifecycle policies and expected cold-recall SLAs, and which upstream services will own/emit canonical fields and tenant/region routing metadata.

EU tenants require EU residency and 7‑year retention; customers accept pseudonymous IDs for historical data; infra provides region-specific managed KMS and object stores; we must avoid reversible leaks and support legal-hold/re-identification workflows under strict controls. 3) Key options: A) Pseudonymize in the Event Aggregation Service using deterministic irreversible HMACs keyed per-tenant (and per-region for EU) with no reversible mapping in the feed store; B) Pseudonymize at source services before events hit the bus (PII never leaves origin); C) Store reversible mappings in a separate encrypted, access-controlled “re-id” vault for legal re-identification. 4) Trade-offs: A (simple central point, consistent pseudonyms, easier to enforce regional keys) risks raw PII already existing upstream but keeps feed stores safe and is operationally straightforward; B maximizes PII minimization but requires changes across services and guarantees upstream compliance; C meets legal re-id needs but increases risk of accidental leakage and operational complexity unless guarded by strong dual-control, audit, and region-bound keys. 5) Recommendation and justification: Adopt A as primary (pseudonymize in Event Aggregation Service post-normalization, before writing to read shards and cold archives) using deterministic HMAC(id || tenant_id || region) with tenant- and region-scoped KMS keys (EU keys resident in EU), never store raw identifiers in feed read stores or exports by default, expose in payloads a consistent pseudonym field (user_pseudonym) plus metadata user_redacted=true and an optional user_display_hint for operational context (e.g., role/title) that omits direct identifiers; implement a separate, tightly governed re-id vault only if legal process requires re-identification (encrypted mappings, dual-approval access, regionally resident, full audit trail), deliver bulk exports from region-resident object stores as pseudonymized by default with time-limited signed URLs and export manifests indicating pseudonymization state, and include immutable region-resident access logs for every read/stream/export. 6) Follow-ups/validations needed: confirm upstream retention/raw-PII location and legal-hold needs (do we need re-id vault at all), specify required fields that may remain as non-identifying display hints, confirm tenant/key management model and KMS per-region boundaries, define exact export contract/schema flags for pseudonymization and re-id request process, and determine operational controls (dual control, CI checks, code review policies, scanning) to prevent accidental re-identification.
